summary_points: Document details including client, project, and revision information.
Important installation instructions include removing orange parts, checking tightness, notifying LOINTEK, and being cautious when entering system.
Table of contents outlines sections on shipping/installation, start-up/operation, maintenance/reparations, and documentation.
Caution section emphasizes the risks of removing covers without proper venting and draining.
Oil to Salt Heat Exchangers shipped with nitrogen gas for shipping.
Inspect for shipping damage immediately upon arrival.
Heaters should be stored on cribbing, not in contact with the ground.
Nitrogen blanketed heaters need regular inspection and pressure restoration.
Install each heater as shown on the General Arrangement Drawing.
Use nylon slings for lifting operations to avoid damaging equipment.
Do not confuse pulling lugs with lifting lugs during handling.
Proper rigging required for lifting Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger Systems
Fixed supports need shims for proper elevation and orientation
Anchor bolt stakeout must match equipment drill distribution
All bolt elements must be correctly installed before lifting
Pipelines should be blown before welding to equipment
Nitrogen protection is crucial for corrosion prevention
Any alterations or repairs must be made under LOINTEK direction
Initial start-up involves filling heat exchangers with preheated HTF and gradually increasing temperature.
Warm start-up requires maintaining specific temperatures and flow rates to ensure proper operation.
Shutdown sequence should prioritize stopping hot fluid before cold side flow.
Preventive measures like nitrogen blanketing are necessary for extended shutdowns.
Field welding requires certified welders and procedures qualified by a Notified Body.
Shell removal involves careful handling to prevent damage, using cribbing and pulling lugs in steps.
Reinstalling the shell requires thorough inspection and proper alignment before insertion.
Bolted connections should have clean surfaces and gaskets free of defects.
Bolted connections should be tightened uniformly in a diametrically staggered pattern.
Gasket selection must follow original design specifications.
Visual examination of tubesheet, tube ends, and inlet pass is recommended.
Penetrant test can detect damages in weldings between the tube and the tubesheet.
Instructions cover plugging of Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger tubes in three categories: tube-end, safety, and tubesheet.
General preparation includes obtaining plugs from Lointek Procedure and cleaning the work area.
Welded plugs require specific precautions such as clean welding areas and avoiding free machining materials.
Tests for plugged tubes include bubble leak tests, penetrant examinations, and optional hydrostatic tests.
Pass partition cover plates can be removed using handles or nuts depending on access type.
Installation involves visual inspection, cleaning, and proper gasket handling to ensure proper sealing.
Hydrostatic test pressures must not be exceeded and should be verified on the nameplate.
Water temperature for hydrostatic testing should be at least 60°F (15.5°C). Check ASME code for minimum temperature.
After filling, hold for one-half hour, drain a sample, and check temperature before proceeding.
Recommended to witness hydrostatic tests by the owner's Authorized Inspector and Notify Body.
